conviction_note: Sum of four findings (-4.5, -2.0, +1.5, +2.0). Deliberately far inside the 13.7% median historical reaction because nothing I found is extraordinary: the guidance bridge is the only hard item, the CFO-timing angle overlaps it, and both are partly offset by a genuinely mixed peer read-across and by the fact that the -29.2% 20-day run-up already contains the August S&P downgrade to CCC+.

findings.finding: FY27 guidance requires a four-point inflection in the revenue trend starting in the quarter being reported: FY26 total revenue was $512.7m less $108.9m of Global Knowledge equals ~$403.8m of continuing (TDS) revenue, so the $388-406m FY27 guide brackets flat; Q1 FY27 was $94.5m, -4.7% YoY, which leaves the guide midpoint needing Q2-Q4 at about -0.7% versus a Q1 running at -4.7% and a company that itself flagged 'softness in government bookings' and consumer down 21%.
findings.why_not_priced: There is effectively no sell-side model on this name to embed the bridge. Market cap is ~$60m (8.97m shares at $6.66), 20-day average volume is 44,231 shares (~$295k/day), there is no listed option chain at all, and the only rating action reported in August was Weiss Ratings — an algorithmic service — moving from 'sell (e+)' to 'sell (d-)'. If the market had done this arithmetic there would be a published Q2-Q4 revenue bridge and a visible estimate cut after the June 9 reaffirmation; instead the calendar carries a single estimate. The GK divestiture leg of the arithmetic is priced (the guide already excludes GK); the required inflection is not.
findings.independence: Company's own Q1 FY27 release and call give the -4.7%/-21% consumer/government-softness inputs (https://investor.skillsoft.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/453/skillsoft-reports-financial-results-for-the-first-quarter-of-fiscal-2027, 2026-06-09), and the FY26 base is from the Q4 FY26 release (https://investor.skillsoft.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/447/skillsoft-reports-financial-results-for-the-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-of-fiscal-2026, 2026-04-07). S&P independently models 'fiscal 2027 revenues near $400 million', i.e. the bottom half of the guide.

findings.finding: Q2 FY27 (May 1 - Jul 31, 2026) is new CFO Ron Kisling's first full quarter — he started 2026-05-20, twenty days before the June 9 reaffirmation — and his predecessor John Frederick's transition-advisory contract expired 2026-09-04, five days before this print, so the first quarter he can fully own is the first one reported without the author of the inherited guidance still under contract.
findings.why_not_priced: The wire reported 'Skillsoft appoints new CFO' in May and moved on; what it did not report is the calendar arithmetic — that the outgoing CFO's advisory engagement was written to end September 4 and this print is September 9. Nobody has published the Kisling-inherits-Frederick's-guide framing. If it were priced you would see it in a preview note; there are no covering previews on a $60m nano-cap with no options.
findings.independence: Partly overlapping with finding 1 — this is the same outcome (a guidance reset) via different evidence, so I have sized it only as the incremental probability shift, not as a standalone -6%. Scorer should treat findings 1 and 2 as one bet with two sources. Confirming detail on Frederick's September 4 end date: https://investor.skillsoft.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/451/skillsoft-appoints-ron-kisling-as-chief-financial-officer (2026-05-20).

findings.finding: The two enterprise-learning comps that reported after Skillsoft last spoke on June 9 disagree with each other, and the closer pure-play comp is the positive one: Docebo (2026-08-07) reported ARR +9.5% YoY, a second consecutive quarter of re-acceleration, and RAISED full-year revenue guidance by $3.5m citing enterprise strength, while Coursera (2026-07-29) reported enterprise NRR down to 91% on L&D budget pressure.
findings.why_not_priced: The sweep row correctly notes the 'corporate-learning-disrupted-by-AI' bear case is fully written up and standing. What is written up is the thesis, not a test of it — and the post-June-9 evidence fails to confirm it. If the market had processed Docebo's raise as a read-across, SKIL would not have fallen 29% over the same 20 days into a print with no offsetting company-specific news. I file this as a small positive precisely because the negative leg (Coursera) exists and I am netting them rather than filing only the leg that suits me.
findings.independence: The offsetting negative leg is Coursera's Q2, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729966984/en/Coursera-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results (2026-07-29, date verified from the URL path 20260729). Both dates verified from URL paths, not snippets.

findings.finding: Tonight is the first call at which a refinancing update is contractually due: on 2026-06-09 Hovsepian said addressing the debt maturities becomes 'management's top financial priority' once the Global Knowledge sale closes, and it closed 2026-07-06 — a $574.6m term loan due 2028-07-16 against $115.6m cash and a ~$60m equity, so any constructive statement is worth far more in percentage terms than silence costs.
findings.why_not_priced: The asymmetry, not the fact, is the finding. The bad branch is already in the tape: the -29.22% 20-day run-up starts within a day of the S&P downgrade to CCC+/negative, which was explicitly about refinancing risk into the 2028 maturity. A market that had also priced a constructive branch would not have this equity at 4.5x EV/EBITDA on the company's own $108-116m guide. With no option chain there is no skew to fade and no volatility premium being paid for the branch, so I score it as a positive-mean, very-wide-band event rather than a direction.
findings.independence: S&P's downgrade to CCC+ from B- with a negative outlook, explicitly on 'high leverage and refinancing risk ahead of the company's 2028 debt maturity' and flagging distressed-transaction risk: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/sp-downgrades-skillsoft-rating-on-high-leverage-concerns-93CH-4856328 (reported 2026-08-12; the URL carries no date path, but the article's own content references the completed Enduring Ventures divestiture and April 2026 cash, so it is internally dated to after 2026-07-06). Primary S&P page https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3610614 returned HTTP 403.

searched_and_found_nothing: Federal contract exposure via USAspending: SKILLSOFT (US) LLC shows $19.54m of lifetime prime obligations over 74 transactions — immaterial against ~$400m of revenue, so the 'softness in government bookings' the company flagged cannot be tracked or sized from prime award data

SC 13D/13G activity in 2026: EDGAR full-text search returns zero 13D/G filings mentioning Skillsoft between 2026-01-01 and 2026-09-09; the Naspers/Prosus and Warburg filings are all 2021-2022. No activist, no take-private stake building

Form 4 cluster on 2026-09-03: three filings, all routine RSU compensation grants (Cushing 55,000, Barbour 40,000, granted 2026-09-01, four- and two-year vesting). No open-market buying or selling, no signal
Codecademy curriculum-team layoffs: real but dated 2026-02-20, two prints ago, already absorbed by the April 7 and June 9 reactions
Secondary-market trading level of the $574.6m term loan — the single most informative datapoint for a residual-claim equity — is not obtainable from public sources; no LCD/LPC quote found
Percipio customer sentiment on G2/Trustpilot/Capterra/Reddit: generic and undated complaints about pricing and AI-generated content quality, nothing quantified or timestamped to Q2 FY27

NYSE 802.01B listing compliance: notice received 2026-03-26, remediation plan accepted 2026-07-08 with an 18-month cure — resolved and disclosed, not a live catalyst, though at $59.7m market cap the company sits only ~16% above the $50m threshold
Skillsoft careers/job board: skillsoft.com returned HTTP 403 to the fetch, so no hiring-trend read

Any 8-K between 2026-08-27 (a director resignation, explicitly not over a disagreement) and today — the filing stream is empty, so the late-August continuation of the decline has no disclosed cause and is most likely illiquidity drift on 44k shares/day
baseline_tension: My net is mildly negative and that cuts against the free control the repo's own analysis prefers — a -29.22% 20-day run-up means -run_up_20d says buy — and it cuts against my own finding that the run-up is explained by the August S&P downgrade and is therefore already-absorbed bad news; it agrees only with the reaction base rate of five consecutive negative prints, which is baseline and not edge, which is why I have sized to -3.0 rather than anywhere near the 13.7% median magnitude.
